title: Choose your online income model and get work-ready

say: Choose your online income model, and get work-ready.
This is the video for module 1 of Digital Entrepreneurship and Remote Work.
People say make money online as if it were one thing. It is not. There are four models, and each pays, grows and fails differently.

panel.heading: Four ways to earn online
items: Remote job: one employer, steady salary
Freelancing: many clients, uneven income
E-commerce: real goods sold online
Digital products: make once, sell many times

say: A remote job means working for one organisation from home. The income is predictable, but the employer sets your hours and tasks, and competition is strong.

panel.heading: Four ways to earn online
items: Remote job: one employer, steady salary
Freelancing: many clients, uneven income
E-commerce: real goods sold online
Digital products: make once, sell many times

say: A freelancer sells a service to several clients, by project or on a retainer, which is a fixed monthly fee for ongoing work. You choose your clients, but income goes up and down.

panel.heading: Four ways to earn online
items: Remote job: one employer, steady salary
Freelancing: many clients, uneven income
E-commerce: real goods sold online
Digital products: make once, sell many times

say: E-commerce means selling physical goods online. You need money for stock, and you still pack and deliver. The internet widens your market, but it does not remove the work of a shop.

panel.heading: Four ways to earn online
items: Remote job: one employer, steady salary
Freelancing: many clients, uneven income
E-commerce: real goods sold online
Digital products: make once, sell many times

say: A digital product, like a budget template or a recipe e-book, is made once and sold many times. But sales start slowly, because people must first find and trust you.

say: Be careful of offers that promise big daily earnings for simple online tasks, or ask for an activation fee. Real employers and clients pay you. They do not charge you to start.

say: Guessing your data use means running out in the middle of a client call. So measure it on your phone's data usage screen.

panel.heading: Amina's monthly data budget
items: One work week on the data screen: 3.2 GB
Four weeks: 3.2 x 4 = 12.8 GB
Add 25% for extra calls: 12.8 x 1.25 = 16 GB
Choose a plan of at least 16 GB
Keep a small top-up on a second SIM

say: A client abroad does not see NEPA or a weak network. They only see late work. So charge everything the night before an important call or deadline.

cards.d: Phone, laptop and power bank charged before every big call or deadline.
Use two networks. When one is weak, switch your hotspot to the other.
Turn on offline access in Google Docs. Keep client files in Google Drive with 2-Step Verification.

say: Use two SIMs on different networks, so you can switch when one is weak.

say: Power often returns with a surge, so use a surge protector or stabiliser. Do not overload one extension socket. Keep cables away from water and from where children walk. And switch off and unplug during heavy lightning storms.

panel.heading: Keep your equipment and home safe
items: Surge protector or stabiliser for laptops
Do not overload one extension socket
Cables away from water and children
Unplug during heavy lightning storms

say: A meeting at 3pm means nothing until you know whose 3pm. Nigeria uses West Africa Time, UTC plus 1, and never changes its clocks. The UK and the US do.

panel.heading: Finding the overlap with a client
items: Nigeria is WAT, UTC+1, all year
New York in July: 5 hours behind Lagos
Client's 9am to 5pm = 2pm to 10pm WAT
Overlap with 9am to 6pm WAT: 2pm to 6pm
Propose: 3pm WAT / 10am New York time

say: To remember. Pick one model that fits your life now. Budget your data from real numbers. Keep backups for power and internet.
Always write both time zones. And publish your working hours with a reply time you can keep every day, for example within one working day.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Start with one model that fits your hours and money
Measure data for a week, times 4, plus a margin
Two SIMs, a power bank and offline mode
Write both time zones when proposing a meeting
Publish hours and a reply time you can keep
